title: Dedicated capacity fair-share allocation, transient-burst safety, and on-call playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD to define fair-share allocation for reserved GPU pools, transient burst safety controls, and an on-call runbook for capacity incidents. This document clarifies requirements, boundaries, acceptance criteria, and rollout strategy for a combinable feature set that reduces noisy-neighbor impact while preserving predictable burst behavior for customers with reserved capacity.
background: Customers using Redwood Dedicated request both predictable reserved throughput and occasional transient bursts. Current behavior can allow a single noisy tenant to consume disproportionate burst headroom causing increased latency for co-tenants and SLA violations. Existing PRDs cover reserved pools, autoscale, and burst governance separately; this PRD synthesizes a fair-share admission model, safety limits, accounting for reserved vs burst budgets, and an on-call playbook for capacity anomalies.
goals: Provide a deterministic fair-share allocator for concurrent burst requests within a reserved GPU pool
Limit per-tenant transient burst impact to preserve SLOs for other tenants on the same pool
Offer controls for admins to configure conservative vs permissive burst policies per pool
Ship a lightweight on-call playbook and automated incident detection for burst-induced SLO degradation
Ensure billing/metrics correctly reflect reserved vs burst usage and correlate to cost reports
scope_in: Fair-share admission controller that enforces CPU/GPU slot shares and token-rate caps during burst windows
Burst budget tracking per tenant (rolling 1h and 24h windows) and pool-wide headroom control
Safety caps: per-tenant max burst concurrency and maximum sustained burst multiplier (configurable; default 1.25x reserved throughput)
APIs and console controls to set pool policy: conservative, balanced, permissive, and emergency-drain
Observable metrics: burst_events, fairshare_denials, per_tenant_burst_utilization, pool_headroom_pct, latency_p50/p90/p99 under burst
On-call playbook with automated alert thresholds and triage steps
scope_out: Changes to model quantization, kernel selection, or low-level serving runtime optimizations (handled by runtime team separately)
Billing pricing changes (billing team will map metrics to billing in a follow-up ticket)
Cross-region capacity migration automation (out of scope for this iteration)
Private control plane full RBAC redesign (only policy knobs exposed in console are included)
requirements: R1: Fair-share algorithm must guarantee 95% of reserved SLOs for non-burst traffic when aggregate pool utilization <= 85%
R2: Per-tenant burst concurrency limit default = 10 concurrent burst sessions; configurable per-customer and per-pool
R3: Burst multiplier default = 1.25x reserved throughput for up to 60 seconds; supports override up to 2x for permissive pools
R4: Admission controller must respond within 50ms for each admission decision to avoid adding noticeable tail latency
R5: All burst decisions (allow/deny/throttle) must be logged to the audit stream and visible in console trace for 30 days
R6: Console must expose per-pool policy with three presets and one emergency toggle to drain burst headroom
R7: Metrics exported to observability pipeline every 15s: per-tenant_burst_tokens, pool_headroom_pct, fairness_index (0-1), and denial_reasons
R8: Automated alerts: trigger P1 when pool_p99_latency increases >25% relative to baseline for 5m and at least 10% of requests are fairshare_denied
R9: Integration test suite that simulates 50 tenants with synthetic burst patterns and validates SLO retention and fairness index >= 0.7
acceptance_criteria: AC1: When running the integration load test (50 tenants, enforced burst patterns), at least 90% of tenants with reserved capacity see p99 latency within 1.2x baseline for non-burst traffic
AC2: Fairness index (Jain's fairness adapted) across tenants >= 0.7 in balanced and permissive presets; >= 0.85 in conservative preset
AC3: Admission decisions are logged and surfaced in console traces and match the audit log for 100% of sampled requests (sample size 10k)
AC4: Default policy prevents any single tenant from consuming >35% of pool burst headroom during a 60s window when more than 3 tenants are active
AC5: Automated alerts fire correctly during induced SLO degradation and on-call runbook resolves simulated incidents within 30 minutes in 4/5 trial runs
AC6: No performance regression in non-burst baseline: token throughput and median latency for non-burst requests remains within 5% of pre-change baseline in production-like test harness
success_metrics: Reduction in pool-level SLO incidents caused by noisy bursts by >= 70% over 90 days
Median time to mitigation for capacity incidents decreases from current baseline by 40% (tracked via incident platform)
95th percentile fairshare_denied rate <= 5% for customers configured with permissive policy
Customer satisfaction (NPS follow-up) for Dedicated customers improves by +7 points on capacity reliability question in next quarterly survey
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): Deploy to 5 small test pools with conservative preset; run integration test harness and customer-simulated traffic
Phase 2 (pilot, 4 weeks): Enable on 10 pilot customer pools (opt-in) with console visibility and forced telemetry collection
Phase 3 (gradual rollout, 6 weeks): Gradual enablement across dedicated pools with default conservative policy, expose console opt-in for permissive presets
Phase 4 (monitor & iterate): 30-day monitoring window, collect regressions, tune defaults; enable emergency-drain toggle in console for SREs
Rollback criteria: >5 P1 incidents attributable to fair-share admission in 24h or average p99 latency degradation >30% for non-burst traffic across multiple pools
risks: Risk: Overly conservative defaults could starve customers relying on burst for spikes; mitigate by opt-in permissive presets and customer communication
Risk: False positives in admission denial causing unexpected 429s; mitigate by telemetry, sample tracing and a gradual rollout
Risk: Added admission latency could increase tail latency; mitigate by enforcing 50ms decision SLAs and benchmarking on representative hardware
Risk: Billing mismatch between reserved vs burst usage; mitigate by cross-team sync with billing to map new metrics before GA
decisions: Decision: Use rolling-window token budgets (1h and 24h) rather than fixed daily quotas to preserve elasticity for short spikes
Decision: Default burst multiplier set to 1.25x to balance freedom vs safety; conservative preset enforces 1.0x, permissive up to 2.0x
Decision: Expose three policy presets in Console and one emergency drain toggle for SREs; not exposing fine-grained per-request hooks in initial launch
Decision: Admission controller lives in the request routing layer to minimize RTT for decisions and to centralize logging
open_questions: Q1: Should burst budgets be transferrable between pools owned by the same tenant? Needs legal/billing sign-off
Q2: How do we surface anticipated denial reasons in SDK responses without leaking internal policy details? Security to advise
Q3: What is the billing model for permissive overrides (chargeable burst credit) — billing team to propose mapping
